title: onsemi Embedded Power Platform Announced
gist: onsemi announced its Embedded Power Platform at investor day: heterogeneous power dies embedded in silicon and linked by wafer-level redistribution layers instead of wire bonds, targeting vehicle electrification and AI power infrastructure. Subaru is the first strategic technology engagement partner, but the near-term flagship use case is an 800V DC AI rack digital breaker replacing bulky electromechanical breakers at several-hundred-kW scale.

insights.claim: onsemi used its investor day to introduce the Embedded Power Platform (EPP), a power-integration approach that embeds heterogeneous power dies into silicon and connects them via wafer-level redistribution layers rather than wire bonds.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: A packaging-level change in power semis is being pitched to investors as a growth vector into AI datacenter power, not just automotive.
insights.quote: a power-integration approach that embeds heterogeneous power dies into silicon and connects them through wafer-level redistribution layers instead of wire bonds

insights.claim: Replacing wire bonds with wafer-level metallization and precision redistribution layers brings semiconductor-fab precision to power interconnects, lowering parasitic inductance for better device control and higher switching frequencies.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Higher switching frequency shrinks passives and magnetics, which is the lever that reduces power-shelf and board area in dense AI racks.
insights.quote: wafer-level metallization replaces wire bonds with precision redistribution layers, bringing semiconductor-fab precision to the interconnects and lowering parasitic inductance
insights.locator: Under the hood / Wafer-Level Metallization section

insights.claim: The platform is presented as technology-agnostic across semiconductor materials and power levels, supporting silicon, SiC, GaN, and future technologies in configurable power-device combinations.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Material-agnostic packaging hedges the SiC-versus-GaN bet and lets one platform be sold into multiple end markets.
insights.quote: onsemi says the platform is technology-agnostic and scales across semiconductor materials and power levels.

insights.claim: EPP integrates drivers and controllers directly with the power devices to reduce system-level complexity, moving value from discrete board-level components into the package.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Package-level integration captures BOM content that previously went to separate driver and controller suppliers.
insights.quote: it integrates drivers and controllers directly with the power devices to reduce system-level complexity

insights.claim: The silicon-based package is built on existing fab and simulation infrastructure located in upstate New York, which the company argues shortens time to market while providing high-voltage isolation and a lower-resistance thermal path.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Using existing domestic fab capacity lowers the capex and execution risk of scaling a new packaging platform.
insights.quote: which onsemi says shortens time to market and provides high-voltage isolation along with a lower-resistance thermal path

themes.theme: Power density as the binding design constraint

insights.claim: Power density has become a hard constraint in vehicle electrification and AI power infrastructure, and the traditional practice of optimizing electrical, thermal, and mechanical design separately has run out of room.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Frames power packaging as a bottleneck market where suppliers that co-optimize physics domains can command share.
insights.quote: power density has become a hard constraint and the traditional practice of optimizing electrical, thermal, and mechanical design separately has run out of room

insights.claim: When electrical, mechanical, and thermal systems are tuned separately, gains in one area create trade-offs elsewhere and force costly late-stage design changes.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Late-stage redesign cost is the pain point EPP monetizes; it also explains why customers would switch packaging vendors.
insights.quote: improvements in one area create trade-offs elsewhere and force costly late-stage design changes
insights.locator: onsemi frames the launch around power density

insights.claim: Full-footprint thermal conduction improves heat dissipation and supports higher continuous power operation, while in-package high-voltage isolation cuts reliance on thermally inefficient insulating materials.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Removing thermally inefficient isolation layers is a direct path to higher rack-level power per unit volume.
insights.quote: high-voltage isolation integrated in the package cuts reliance on thermally inefficient insulating materials

insights.claim: Digital twin simulation with multi-physics co-optimization lets engineers iterate designs quickly, reducing the number of hardware builds and shortening development cycles.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Simulation-led design is becoming a competitive moat in power semis, echoing what EDA did for logic.
insights.quote: digital twin simulation with multi-physics co-optimization lets engineers iterate designs quickly, reducing hardware builds and shortening development cycles

themes.theme: 800V AI racks and the digital breaker use case

insights.claim: Although the announcement is framed around automotive, the first major use case is expected to target 800V DC AI racks.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Signals that AI datacenter power, not EVs, may be the near-term revenue driver for this platform.
insights.quote: it sounds like the first major use case will be targeting 800V DC AI racks

insights.claim: onsemi described replacing a bulky electromechanical breaker for a several-hundred-kW 800V rack with a much smaller digital breaker that can be liquid- or air-cooled, controlled, and instrumented for telemetry.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Solid-state protection at several-hundred-kW rack scale is a new, non-GPU silicon content category inside AI racks.
insights.quote: imagine this solution as a much smaller digital breaker, with a way to easily liquid-cool (or air-cool) it, control it, and get telemetry data out of the assembly

insights.claim: In AI data centers, higher power density frees board and rack space and enables thermally efficient, compact power delivery.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Rack space freed by denser power conversion can be resold as compute density, which is how power vendors justify price premiums.
insights.quote: In AI data centers, higher power density frees board and rack space and enables thermally efficient, compact power delivery.
insights.locator: onsemi targets vehicle electrification and AI power infrastructure first

insights.claim: EPP addresses a different part of the rack power problem than liquid-cooled 800V DC busbars from vendors such as Wiwynn and TE Connectivity, which handle delivering power through the rack, whereas EPP integrates power devices, interconnects, and control functions inside a package.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Maps the 800V rack value chain into distinct, separately investable layers: distribution versus in-package conversion and protection.
insights.quote: EPP addresses a different part of that problem by integrating power devices, interconnects, and control functions within a package.

insights.claim: Next-generation rack optimization is moving beyond GPUs, NICs, CPUs, switches, storage, and liquid cooling and into power delivery itself.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Points investors toward power-chain suppliers as the next area of AI-rack content growth after cooling.
insights.quote: AI racks are getting denser, so optimization for next-generation racks is going beyond GPUs, NICs, CPUs, switches, storage, and liquid cooling and into power delivery.

insights.claim: The same 800V platform architecture is being leveraged across both automotive and AI data centers, creating shared engineering and volume across two very different end markets.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Cross-market reuse of 800V designs could let auto-heavy power semi vendors ride AI capex without building a new product line.
insights.quote: Interestingly, 800V platforms are being leveraged across automotive and AI data centers.

insights.claim: Subaru signed on as the first strategic technology engagement partner, receiving early access to engineering samples, simulation models, and technical expertise to evaluate the platform for next-generation vehicle architectures.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: A named OEM evaluation is the first external validation signal, but it is an evaluation, not a design win.
insights.quote: Subaru has entered a strategic technology engagement with onsemi to evaluate EPP for next-generation vehicle architectures.

insights.claim: The Subaru arrangement is explicitly a customer evaluation engagement because automotive design cycles are long, implying automotive revenue is further out than the datacenter opportunity.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Sets expectations that any EPP revenue inflection likely shows up in AI power infrastructure before automotive.
insights.quote: This is a customer evaluation engagement since automotive usually has a longer design cycle.

insights.claim: Beyond automotive and AI, the architecture is positioned to address fast-charging infrastructure, energy storage, grid modernization, and industrial automation.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: A broad addressable-market claim that spreads the platform's payback across multiple electrification cycles.
insights.quote: the architecture also covers fast-charging infrastructure, energy storage, grid modernization, and industrial automation
insights.locator: Enabling the Next Generation of Power Systems

insights.claim: Lower inductance enabling faster switching plus full-footprint thermal conduction is claimed to support smaller, lighter traction inverters that scale across vehicle platforms.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Inverter weight and size reduction is a measurable OEM purchasing criterion, making the claim testable against future design wins.
insights.quote: Lower inductance enables faster switching, and full-footprint thermal conduction supports smaller, lighter traction inverters that scale across vehicle platforms.
insights.locator: onsemi targets vehicle electrification and AI power infrastructure first
